facts.title: Akwe:kon
facts.summary: Akwe:kon, the first Native student residence hall in North America, is offered alongside Indigenous Studies courses and student leadership opportunities.
facts.hook: offers a home at Akwe:kon, the first Native student residence hall in North America
facts.quote: Indigenous Studies (AIIS) courses, student leadership opportunities, and an undergraduate residential experience at Akwe:kon, the first Native student residence hall in North America.
facts.sourceTitle: Belonging & Inclusion | Undergraduate Admissions
facts.commonnessReason: Listed on the admissions belonging page.

facts.title: Cornell Atkinson Center for Sustainability
facts.summary: Cornell's hub for collaborative sustainability research, connecting researchers, students, staff, and outside partners.
facts.hook: connects students and researchers across Cornell on sustainability research
facts.quote: The Cornell Atkinson Center for Sustainability is the hub of collaborative sustainability research at Cornell University, forging vital connections among researchers, students, staff and external partners.
facts.sourceTitle: Affiliated Centers | School of Civil and Environmental Engineering | Cornell Duffield Engineering
facts.commonnessReason: Cornell's flagship sustainability center; many environment-focused applicants name it.

facts.title: David M. Einhorn Center for Community Engagement
facts.summary: Cornell's community engagement center supports courses and co-curricular programs so that undergraduates learn to partner with communities.
facts.hook: supports community-engaged courses and programs across the university
facts.quote: At the Einhorn Center, we’re making high-quality community-engaged learning a hallmark of a Cornell education. We want every undergraduate student to learn how to partner with communities to create a better world, and we support programs across the university — from courses to co-curricular activities — that advance this goal.
facts.sourceTitle: Einhorn Center for Community Engagement
facts.commonnessReason: Featured on admissions pages as Cornell's community engagement hub.

facts.title: Entrepreneurship at Cornell
facts.summary: A university-wide entrepreneurship program that runs conferences, hackathons, internships, mentorship, a business accelerator, co-working spaces, and competitions.
facts.hook: runs hackathons, mentorship, a business accelerator, and competitions for student founders
facts.quote: Entrepreneurship at Cornell (EaC) is a university-wide program ... like big conferences, hackathons, internship and mentorship programs, webinars, a business accelerator, and wonderful co-working spaces and competitions
facts.sourceTitle: Entrepreneurship at Cornell - Entrepreneurship at Cornell
facts.commonnessReason: Most universities have an entrepreneurship hub; applicants interested in startups often cite it.

facts.title: Health Professions Advising Center (HPAC)
facts.summary: Cornell's Health Professions Advising Center serves all students interested in pre-health, from early exploration through preparing for and applying to pre-health programs.
facts.hook: advises any Cornell student exploring, preparing for, or applying to pre-health programs
facts.quote: Cornell’s resource for all students interested in pre-health is the Health Professions Advising Center (HPAC) office and website. This office serves students interested in a variety of pre-health professional pathways and assists students at various stages of exploration, preparing for, and applying to pre-health programs.
facts.sourceTitle: Pre-Health Pathways | Cornell Duffield Engineering
facts.commonnessReason: Pre-health advising offices are standard at most universities.

facts.title: John S. Knight Institute for Writing in the Disciplines
facts.nameOnPage: John S. Knight Institute for Writing in the Disciplines
facts.summary: The Knight Institute runs Cornell's First-Year Writing Seminar Program, which serves the vast majority of first-year students, and its Writing Workshop offers writing classes and tutoring.
facts.hook: runs the first-year writing seminars and a Writing Workshop with tutoring for all writers
facts.quote: The Knight Institute coordinates the First-Year Writing Seminar Program, which serves the vast majority of first-year students at Cornell. ... The Knight Institute is also home to the Writing Workshop, which offers tutorial-based writing classes and tutoring services for writers at all levels, disciplines, and stages of the writing process.
facts.sourceTitle: John S. Knight Institute for Writing in the Disciplines | John S. Knight Institute for Writing in the Disciplines
facts.commonnessReason: First-Year Writing Seminars are a standard part of the Cornell curriculum.

facts.title: Latina/o Studies Program and Latino Living Center
facts.summary: The Latina/o Studies Program welcomes all students to its academic and cultural events and includes the Latino Living Center, an intercultural residential program house.
facts.hook: offers Latina/o studies events and an intercultural program house, the Latino Living Center
facts.quote: All Cornell students are welcome to participate in the Latina/o Studies Program’s academic and socio-cultural events. ... its intercultural residential program house, the Latino Living Center. The Living Center provides students from many cultural backgrounds with a safe and supportive environment where Latino cultures and worldviews are valued.
facts.sourceTitle: Belonging & Inclusion | Undergraduate Admissions
facts.commonnessReason: Listed on the admissions belonging page.

facts.title: New York State Water Resources Institute
facts.nameOnPage: New York State Water Resources Institute
facts.summary: The New York State Water Resources Institute at Cornell connects researchers, water managers, policymakers, and the public to improve water management through research, funding, and outreach.
facts.hook: links Cornell water research with New York agencies, managers, and community groups
facts.quote: At the New York State Water Resources Institute at Cornell University (NYSWRI), we support robust science and dialogue between researchers, managers, policymakers, and the general public to improve water management through: ... Relationship-building with state agencies, professional organizations, and citizen stakeholder groups.
facts.sourceTitle: New York State Water Resources Institute | CALS

facts.title: BEE 4670: Applied Water Research In NYS
facts.summary: A seminar series that brings together researchers working with the New York State Water Resources Institute at Cornell and state agency partners to improve water management in New York.
facts.hook: connects students with researchers and state agencies working on New York's water problems
facts.quote: Every year, the New York State Water Resources Institute (NYSWRI) at Cornell supports applied research that addresses critical water resource problems in NYS and the nation. This seminar series brings together researchers who work with NYSWRI and state agency partners to support and improve water management in the state.
facts.sourceTitle: Class Roster - Spring 2027 - BEE 4670

facts.title: CEE 3007: Engineering in the Community
facts.summary: A course in which students plan, design, and build an infrastructure service project for the local community while learning power tools and how to communicate with non-experts.
facts.hook: has students plan, design, and build an infrastructure project for the local community
facts.quote: This course will prepare you for this type of engagement by planning, designing, and building an infrastructure service project to benefit the local community. You will develop skills in using power tools, project management, risk management, engineering judgment, communicating with non-experts, teamwork, and leadership.
facts.sourceTitle: Class Roster - Spring 2027 - CEE 3007

facts.title: CEE 4795: Sensors for the Built and Natural Environments
facts.summary: A course introducing sensors for civil and environmental engineering uses such as air and water quality monitoring and watershed engineering, in which students design and assemble a sensing system.
facts.hook: has students design and assemble sensing systems for air, water, and watershed monitoring
facts.quote: This course introduces students to a wide variety of sensors with a specific focus on civil and environmental engineering applications such as material testing, structural health monitoring, traffic engineering, air and water quality monitoring, structural testing, watershed engineering, and geotechnical and subsurface energy applications. ... Design and assemble a sensing system for a specific measuring/monitoring application
facts.sourceTitle: Class Roster - Spring 2027 - CEE 4795

facts.title: CEE 4800: Engineering Smart Cities
facts.summary: A course on smart city infrastructure in which students combine data and models to control system performance, with case studies in urban flooding, energy supply, air quality, and water supply.
facts.hook: teaches students to combine data and models to run city infrastructure, from flood control to water supply
facts.quote: In particular, students will learn to combine data and models to control overall system performance in the face of uncertainty. ... Finally, the class will explore cases studies in urban flooding, energy supply, transportation and air quality, and water supply.
facts.sourceTitle: Class Roster - Spring 2027 - CEE 4800

facts.title: CRP 4680: Introduction to Urban Data Science: Theory, Applications, and Practice
facts.summary: A city planning course in which students use Python and open-source urban datasets to analyze, visualize, and communicate data for planning and policy questions.
facts.hook: has students analyze open urban datasets in Python and present findings for planning and policy
facts.quote: Urban data science combines questions of urban development, structure, complexity, theory, policy, and dynamics with a set of computational tools and big data. ... Using Python and open-source urban datasets in the Jupyter Notebook environment, students will work on hands-on applied exercises and projects which emphasize framing theoretically grounded and data-driven questions, analyzing and visualizing data, and communicating results for planning and policy contexts.
facts.sourceTitle: Class Roster - Spring 2027 - CRP 4680

facts.title: ENGRD 2400: Observing the Earth: Remote Sensing and GIS
facts.summary: An engineering course that introduces GIS and satellite remote sensing data and ends with a student-designed capstone project analyzing satellite data.
facts.hook: introduces GIS and satellite data analysis through a student-designed capstone project
facts.quote: We will introduce students to Geographical Information Systems (GIS) and other methods for viewing and manipulating data. ... Students will design and present a capstone project involving satellite data analysis and interpretation.
facts.sourceTitle: Class Roster - Spring 2027 - ENGRD 2400

facts.title: ENGRI 1130: Sustainable Engineering of Energy, Water, Soil, and Air Resources
facts.summary: An introductory engineering course organized into energy, water, soil, and air modules, each built around a case study of local or regional significance.
facts.hook: introduces first-year engineers to sustainable resource management through local case studies
facts.quote: Course introduces concepts and tools required for the sustainable management of energy, water, soil, and air resources in our modern society. Semester is organized into four modules, each concentrating on one resource area and including a case study of local or regional significance.
facts.sourceTitle: Class Roster - Spring 2027 - ENGRI 1130

facts.title: ENGRI 1410: How Machines Learn: AI from the Perceptron to GPT
facts.summary: An introductory engineering course on machine learning and neural networks, from the perceptron to GPT-style models, taught with math tools first-year students can use.
facts.hook: introduces first-year engineers to how neural networks learn, from the perceptron to GPT
facts.quote: This course covers learning, deep learning, and neural networks from the perceptron ... The course emphasizes concepts and applications with mathematical tools that freshmen can wield to connect engineering tools with AI methods.
facts.sourceTitle: Class Roster - Spring 2027 - ENGRI 1410

facts.title: ENVS 4500: Climate Solutions Capstone
facts.summary: A capstone in which students carry out a climate action from Project Drawdown's list and work in teams with Cornell Cooperative Extension or Climate Action Now on climate education.
facts.hook: teams students with Cornell Cooperative Extension or Climate Action Now on climate solutions
facts.quote: In this course, you will choose and implement a climate action from Project Drawdown's (www.drawdown.org) list of 82 climate solutions. ... For the capstone team project, you will work with other students and a community partner (Cornell Cooperative Extension or Climate Action Now) to support education related to plant-rich diet, low-emissions agriculture, forest regeneration, or other climate solutions.
facts.sourceTitle: Class Roster - Fall 2026 - ENVS 4500

facts.title: LSP 3250: Vamos Pa'l Norte: U.S. Migration and Communication
facts.summary: A Latina/o Studies course on how communication can reduce or deepen the barriers migrants face in the United States, focused on Latina/o/x immigrant communities.
facts.hook: examines how communication helps or hinders Latina/o/x immigrant communities in the U.S.
facts.quote: Thus, this course will introduce us to different frameworks, research, and practices that can help us understand the important role of communication in different, U.S., migration experiences. On the one hand, communication can help mitigate some of the social and structural barriers that migrants face in the United States and elsewhere. ... The readings and content of this course primarily focus on the experiences of Latina/o/x immigrant communities in the U.S.
facts.sourceTitle: Class Roster - Spring 2027 - LSP 3250

facts.title: MUSIC 4616: Jazz Combos
facts.summary: Cornell's jazz combo course, in which students explore traditional and contemporary styles through ear-based learning and weekly coaching.
facts.hook: places students in jazz combos with weekly coaching on traditional and contemporary styles
facts.quote: Jazz Combos (MUSIC 4616) ... Students explore traditional and contemporary styles through ear-based learning and collaborative rehearsal techniques. Weekly coachings help develop musicianship, creativity, and a personal artistic voice.
facts.sourceTitle: Jazz | Department of Music

facts.title: PE 1666: Bike Touring
facts.summary: A physical education course that teaches bike touring gear, camping, route planning, and bike maintenance, ending in a two-day bike tour with overnight camping.
facts.hook: teaches bike maintenance and route planning, ending with a two-day bike tour
facts.quote: This course will cover bike touring equipment use, camping skills, route planning and bike maintenance. ... the course will culminate in a two-day bike tour with overnight camping.
facts.sourceTitle: Class Roster - Spring 2027 - PE 1666

facts.title: PUBPOL 3015: Climate Economics and Policy
facts.summary: A Brooks School course that applies economics to climate policy, starting with climate-related market failures, the climate policy portfolio, and the history of international climate negotiations.
facts.hook: applies economics to climate policy, from market failures to international climate negotiations
facts.quote: This course applies the tools of economics to the analysis of the climate challenge and climate policy. We will start with an introduction to the multiple market failures relevant to climate change, an overview of the climate policy portfolio, and a history of international climate negotiations.
facts.sourceTitle: Class Roster - Fall 2026 - PUBPOL 3015

facts.title: SPAN 2070: Intermediate Spanish for the Medical and Health Professions
facts.summary: An intermediate Spanish course built on health-related themes that practices real situations such as taking a medical history and speaking with Hispanic patients in a culturally appropriate way.
facts.hook: practices medical Spanish, from taking a patient history to culturally aware doctor-patient talk
facts.quote: Special attention is given to relevant cultural differences and how cultural notions may affect medical care and communication between doctor and patient. The objective of 2070 is to provide practice in real-life application, such as taking a medical history, calming a patient, and how to speak to a Hispanic patient in a culturally acceptable manner.
facts.sourceTitle: Class Roster - Spring 2027 - SPAN 2070

facts.title: DeFrees Hydraulics Lab
facts.summary: The DeFrees Hydraulics Lab anchors Cornell's environmental fluid mechanics and hydrology program, with a wave tank, a wind-water tunnel, and a flume that models rivers, estuaries, and lake shores.
facts.hook: provides wave tanks and flumes that model rivers, estuaries, and lake shorelines
facts.quote: The focal point of research and experimental studies in the environmental fluid mechanics and hydrology program, the DeFrees hydraulics lab is equipped with three main experimental facilities: ... Designed to model shallow coastal waters, rivers, estuaries, the littoral zone of lakes, and more generally any environment where the horizontal length scales are long relative to the depths.
facts.sourceTitle: Educational Facilities | School of Civil and Environmental Engineering | Cornell Duffield Engineering

facts.title: Dilmun Hill Student Farm
facts.summary: A working farm managed by students, who make day-to-day decisions, grow produce for the campus, and build hands-on skills in sustainable agriculture.
facts.hook: lets students run a working farm and grow produce for the campus community
facts.quote: Dilmun Hill is a place where students build hands-on skills in sustainable agriculture, manage a working farm, and grow collaborations and community. ... Student managers lead day-to-day decisions, growing fresh produce for the wider campus community.
facts.sourceTitle: Dilmun Hill Student Farm | CALS

facts.title: Environmental Teaching Lab
facts.summary: A civil and environmental engineering lab for bench-scale analysis of environmental samples that hosts an automated water treatment plant design competition for upper-level undergraduates.
facts.hook: hosts an automated water treatment plant design competition for upper-level undergraduates
facts.quote: This flexible facility is designed for bench scale experiments and analysis of environmental samples and processes. The Environmental Teaching Lab hosts an automated water treatment plant design competition for upper level undergraduates, and a biocatalysis laboratory for graduate students.
facts.sourceTitle: Educational Facilities | School of Civil and Environmental Engineering | Cornell Duffield Engineering

facts.title: Herbert F. Johnson Museum of Art
facts.summary: Cornell's art museum sits at the top of Libe Slope, has free admission, and leads class sessions in its permanent collection galleries.
facts.hook: brings classes into its permanent collection galleries, with free admission for all
facts.quote: Admission is always free and open to all ... The Museum was designed by I. M. Pei and sits at the top of Libe Slope. ... We help design and lead class sessions in our permanent collection galleries and classrooms
facts.sourceTitle: Homepage - Herbert F. Johnson Museum of Art
facts.commonnessReason: A campus landmark featured on admissions pages.

facts.title: Manufacturing and Learning Studio
facts.summary: The Sibley School's professionally staffed machine shop, with milling machines, lathes, and CNC machines, trains everyone who uses it.
facts.hook: trains students to use milling machines, lathes, and CNC machines in a staffed machine shop
facts.quote: The Manufacturing and Learning Studio of the Sibley School of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering is equipped with standard milling machines, lathes, high-end CNC machines, and a host of support equipment, this machine shop is professionally staffed and provides thorough training to all who use it.
facts.sourceTitle: Project Team Facilities | Cornell Duffield Engineering

facts.title: Rapid Prototyping Lab
facts.summary: A student-operated engineering prototyping lab with 3D printers, a laser cutter, and a CNC router table.
facts.hook: gives engineering students 3D printers, a laser cutter, and a CNC router run by fellow undergraduates
facts.quote: Operated by undergraduate engineering students, the Rapid Prototyping Lab provides a variety of 3D printers, a laser cutter, and a CNC router table.
facts.sourceTitle: Project Team Facilities | Cornell Duffield Engineering
facts.commonnessReason: Makerspaces are common across engineering schools; applicants mention them often.

facts.title: Schwartz Center for the Performing Arts
facts.nameOnPage: Schwartz Center for the Performing Arts
facts.summary: Home of the Department of Performing and Media Arts, with four performance spaces, rehearsal studios, scenery, costume, and prop shops, and film editing and production suites.
facts.hook: houses four stages, theater and dance studios, scene shops, and film production suites
facts.quote: Its marble walls encompass all the elements needed for teaching and performance in theatre, film and dance: four performance spaces, dance and theatre rehearsal studios, scenery, costume and prop shops ... and film editing and production suites.
facts.sourceTitle: The Schwartz Center | Performing and Media Arts
facts.commonnessReason: The main performing arts venue, mentioned on admissions pages.

facts.title: Damian Helbling
facts.summary: Damian Helbling, in Cornell's School of Civil and Environmental Engineering, studies organic chemicals in water and wastewater and develops ways to remediate impacted water systems.
facts.hook: researches contaminants in water and wastewater and technologies to clean impacted water systems
facts.quote: His graduate research focused on the use of sensor networks within drinking water distribution systems to monitor and control post-treatment water quality. ... Helbling joined the School of Civil and Environmental Engineering at Cornell University in January 2014. His research has focused on developing techniques to characterize the universe of organic molecules in water and wastewater by means of high-resolution mass spectrometry and developing technologies for the remediation of impacted water systems.
facts.sourceTitle: Damian E. Helbling | Cornell Duffield Engineering

facts.title: Edwin (Todd) Cowen
facts.summary: Todd Cowen directs Cornell's DeFrees Hydraulics Laboratory and studies environmental fluid mechanics, including lake hydrodynamics and how water masses and environmental DNA move in Cayuga Lake.
facts.hook: studies lake hydrodynamics and how water and environmental DNA move through Cayuga Lake
facts.quote: Edwin “Todd” Cowen is the Director of the DeFrees Hydraulics Laboratory ... He has built an environmental fluid mechanics research program centered on five themes: environmental transport processes, water wave induced flows, lake hydrodynamics (physical limnology), energy harvesting, and quantitative imaging techniques. ... the fate, transport and residence time of water masses and environmental DNA in Cayuga Lake
facts.sourceTitle: Edwin (Todd) Cowen | Cornell Duffield Engineering

facts.title: H. Oliver Gao
facts.summary: Oliver Gao researches climate-smart mobility and low-emission infrastructure and directs the Center for Transportation, Environment, and Community Health (CTECH).
facts.hook: leads research on climate-smart transportation, low-emission infrastructure, and community health
facts.quote: His research focuses on advancing climate-smart mobility, low-emission infrastructure, and data-enabled health systems ... As the Director of the Center for Transportation, Environment, and Community Health (CTECH)—a U.S. Department of Transportation University Transportation Center—Gao leads a multi-institutional consortium uniting engineering, environmental science, public health, and data analytics to drive systems innovation for healthy and sustainable communities.
facts.sourceTitle: H. Oliver Gao | Cornell Duffield Engineering

facts.title: Jacqueline Gerson
facts.summary: Jacqueline Gerson, an assistant professor of biological and environmental engineering, teaches water quality from sample collection and data analysis to policies and management strategies.
facts.hook: teaches water quality from sample collection through data analysis to management and policy
facts.quote: Assistant Professor, Biological and Environmental Engineering ... Professor Gerson teaches students about water quality, from sample collection to data analysis and ultimately management of our waters. Her courses examine the physical, chemical, and biological aspects of water quality, and how this information can be leveraged to develop effective polices and management strategies that benefit both human and ecological health.
facts.sourceTitle: Jacqueline Gerson | CALS

facts.title: Albertson Lab
facts.summary: A civil and environmental engineering lab studying how water, CO2, pollutants, and energy move between land and atmosphere, fusing measurements and models for air quality prediction.
facts.hook: fuses field measurements and models to predict land-atmosphere exchange and air quality
facts.quote: Focusing on the development of a comprehensive understanding of the exchange rates of mass (e.g. water, CO2, pollutants), energy, and momentum between the land and atmosphere. Primary applications in hydrometeorology and air quality, particularly focused on the fusion of measurements and models for optimal prediction.
facts.sourceTitle: Research Groups | School of Civil and Environmental Engineering | Cornell Duffield Engineering

facts.title: Critical Infrastructure Systems Lab
facts.summary: A civil and environmental engineering lab that assesses climate risk to interconnected infrastructure and designs management approaches that balance reliability, resilience, and sustainability.
facts.hook: studies how climate risk threatens interconnected infrastructure and how to manage it
facts.quote: CIS Lab works on the interaction between critical infrastructures and the natural environment. Members characterize climate risk on interconnected infrastructure systems and provide adaptive, robust, and scalable management solutions that balance reliability, resilience, and sustainability.
facts.sourceTitle: Research Groups | School of Civil and Environmental Engineering | Cornell Duffield Engineering

facts.title: Reed Research Group
facts.summary: A civil and environmental engineering group studying sustainable water management under competing demands from renewable energy, ecosystems, growing populations, and climate change.
facts.hook: researches how to manage water sustainably as energy, ecosystem, and climate pressures collide
facts.quote: The Reed Research Group’s primary research interests relate to sustainable water management given conflicting demands from renewable energy systems, ecosystem services, expanding populations, and climate change.
facts.sourceTitle: Research Groups | School of Civil and Environmental Engineering | Cornell Duffield Engineering

facts.title: Reid Research Group
facts.summary: A civil and environmental engineering lab that applies environmental biogeochemistry and ecosystem engineering, including nature-based technologies, to water quality problems.
facts.hook: studies nature-based technologies that protect the quality of water resources
facts.quote: Our laboratory is focused on investigating the applications of environmental biogeochemistry and ecosystem engineering to water quality problems. Our group seeks to understand and innovate the use of nature-based technologies as sustainable tools to ensure the quality of water resources for societal needs and ecosystem health.
facts.sourceTitle: Research Groups | School of Civil and Environmental Engineering | Cornell Duffield Engineering

facts.title: Richardson Lab
facts.summary: A civil and environmental engineering lab that studies microbial communities for bioremediation, bioenergy, sustainable wastewater treatment, and pathogen detection.
facts.hook: investigates microbes used for bioremediation, wastewater treatment, and pathogen detection
facts.quote: The Richardson group studies microbial communities of relevance to important environmental engineering problems. Application areas include bioremediation, bioenergy, sustainable wastewater treatment ... and pathogen detection.
facts.sourceTitle: Research Groups | School of Civil and Environmental Engineering | Cornell Duffield Engineering

facts.title: Cayuga Lake
facts.summary: Cayuga Lake, one of the Finger Lakes, gives Cornell students a place for boating, swimming, and fishing.
facts.hook: gives students a Finger Lake for boating, swimming, and fishing
facts.quote: Cayuga Lake is a fantastic place for boating, swimming, fishing, or just watching the sunset. Discover what makes life in the Finger Lakes so unique by taking advantage of our beautiful lake.
facts.sourceTitle: The Cornell Experience | Undergraduate Admissions
facts.commonnessReason: Featured on admissions pages; a standard part of Cornell's setting.

facts.title: Cornell Biological Field Station internships on Oneida Lake
facts.summary: The Cornell Biological Field Station on the south shore of Oneida Lake offers 10-week summer undergraduate research internships with mentor scientists.
facts.hook: offers 10-week summer research internships on Oneida Lake with mentor scientists
facts.quote: The Department of Natural Resources and the Environment, in conjunction with the Cornell Biological Field Station (CBFS), will offer 10-week undergraduate research internships during the summer field season. ... The Cornell Biological Field Station is a well-equipped facility located on the south shore of Oneida Lake, NY.
facts.sourceTitle: CBFS Internship Program | CALS

facts.title: Cornell Botanic Gardens on-campus natural areas
facts.summary: Cornell Botanic Gardens' on-campus natural areas include the Cascadilla Gorge Trail, Beebe Lake's water, woods, and wetlands, and the nearly 200-foot-deep Fall Creek Gorge.
facts.hook: offers gorge trails, Beebe Lake, and wetlands in the heart of campus
facts.quote: The iconic Cascadilla Gorge Trail passes through one of the most picturesque gorges in the Finger Lakes Region. ... Beebe Lake is a sanctuary of water, woods, and wetlands in the heart of the Cornell Campus. ... Nearly 200 feet deep, Fall Creek’s Gorge is among the most impressive gorges in the Finger Lakes Region.
facts.sourceTitle: On-Campus Natural Areas | Cornell Botanic Gardens
facts.commonnessReason: Ithaca's gorges are among the most frequently cited features of Cornell.

facts.title: Finger Lakes PFAS mapping project
facts.summary: Undergraduates in Damian Helbling's research group have sampled more than 300 bodies of water, including all 11 Finger Lakes, for PFAS and added the data to an interactive map.
facts.hook: lets undergraduates sample Finger Lakes waters for PFAS and share results on a public map
facts.quote: A group of undergraduates in Helbling’s research group has since filled the gap, taking more than 500 samples across 300 bodies of water, including all 11 Finger Lakes and many tributaries, ponds and even puddles that persistently pool after rain. They’ve screened the samples for 24 common PFAS and added the data to an interactive map.
facts.sourceTitle: Students create first in-depth map of ‘forever chemicals’ in the Finger Lakes | Cornell Chronicle

facts.title: Biological Sciences Major
facts.summary: Cornell's Biological Sciences major requires each student to declare one of 14 concentrations, among them Neurobiology & Behavior, which explores how nervous systems generate behavior.
facts.hook: lets biology majors specialize in one of 14 concentrations, from neurobiology to marine biology
facts.quote: Biological Sciences 14 concentrations ... All Biological Sciences Majors must declare a concentration. ... Neurobiology & Behavior ... Exploring how nervous systems generate behavior, from neurons to societies.
facts.sourceTitle: Concentrations | CALS
facts.commonnessReason: The main biology major; pre-med and biology applicants often cite it.

facts.title: Environmental Engineering Major
facts.summary: Cornell's B.S. in Environmental Engineering is offered jointly by the College of Engineering and CALS and trains students to prevent or clean up pollution of air, streams, and groundwater.
facts.hook: offers an environmental engineering degree run jointly by the College of Engineering and CALS
facts.quote: They work to contain, reduce or prevent hazardous waste, air pollution, or contaminated streams and groundwater. ... The Bachelor degree program in Environmental Engineering is jointly offered by the College of Engineering and the College of Agriculture and Life Sciences at Cornell University.
facts.sourceTitle: Environmental Engineering Major | School of Civil and Environmental Engineering | Cornell Duffield Engineering
facts.commonnessReason: The intended major's own program page; nearly every environmental engineering applicant cites the major itself.

facts.title: Minor in Sustainable Energy Systems
facts.summary: A six-course minor open to all undergraduates that requires a course in each of four categories, including one on the policy, economics, business, history, and ethics of energy.
facts.hook: pairs energy technology courses with a required policy, economics, or ethics course
facts.quote: The minor is open to all undergraduate students. ... To earn the minor, students must complete six courses and a minimum of 18 credits ... At least one course from each of four breadth categories: ... Category 4: Social Impact: Policy, Economics, Business, History, Ethics, and Risk Analysis
facts.sourceTitle: Minor in Sustainable Energy Systems | Cornell Duffield Engineering

facts.title: Smart Cities Minor
facts.summary: An engineering minor that teaches students to use sensors, real-time data, and AI to design and control dynamic infrastructure systems for future cities.
facts.hook: trains engineers to use sensors, real-time data, and AI to run city infrastructure
facts.quote: The smart cities minor equips engineering students to use sensors, smart devices, real-time data, and AI for designing and controlling dynamic infrastructure systems. It combines technical civil engineering skills with knowledge of the environment, climate change, technology, and data science to help engineer future smart cities.
facts.sourceTitle: Minors in Smart Cities and Engineering Management | School of Civil and Environmental Engineering

facts.title: AguaClara Project Team
facts.summary: AguaClara is a Cornell engineering project team that develops sustainable, gravity-powered water treatment technologies, including an automated coagulant dosing system, for communities worldwide.
facts.hook: develops gravity-powered water treatment technology for communities around the world
facts.quote: I am one of the team leads for the AguaClara Project team, where we develop sustainable, gravity-powered water treatment technologies for communities around the world. We are currently developing an automated coagulant dosing system to eliminate the need for an operator at all times
facts.sourceTitle: Kayla Stephenson '26: From classroom to community | R.F. Smith School of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering
facts.commonnessReason: A well-known Cornell water project team that environmental engineering applicants often find.

facts.title: Cornell GreenClub
facts.summary: A student-led sustainability group, offered with a course, whose interdisciplinary teams design and carry out community-based sustainability projects with campus or community partners.
facts.hook: runs student-led sustainability projects with campus and community partners
facts.quote: This course engages students in real-world, community-based sustainability projects through Cornell GreenClub. Structured as a student-led, engaged-learning experience, students work in interdisciplinary teams to design and implement stakeholder-focused projects that address community needs.
facts.sourceTitle: Class Roster - Spring 2027 - BEE 4950

facts.title: Cornell Speech and Debate
facts.summary: Cornell's only university-sponsored debate organization, competing in policy debate, British Parliamentary debate, Spanish-language Worlds debate, and individual speech events.
facts.hook: competes in policy debate and in Spanish-language Worlds debate
facts.quote: The Cornell Speech and Debate Program is the only university-sponsored debate organization at Cornell. We compete in Policy debate, Worlds (British Parliamentary) debate, Spanish-language Worlds debate and Individual Speech events.
facts.sourceTitle: Cornell Speech and Debate | The ILR School
facts.commonnessReason: The university's main debate program; known but not a typical essay focus.

facts.title: Engineers Without Borders
facts.summary: A Cornell student group that designs and implements sustainable engineering projects with international communities.
facts.hook: lets students design and build sustainable engineering projects with communities abroad
facts.quote: Students who aim to create long-lasting solutions to problems in international communities. Members are given the opportunity to nurture their creative and technical expertise by designing and implementing sustainable engineering projects.
facts.sourceTitle: Clubs and Organizations | School of Civil and Environmental Engineering | Cornell Duffield Engineering
facts.commonnessReason: Engineers Without Borders chapters exist at many universities.

facts.title: Jazz Ensemble (MUSIC 4615)
facts.summary: Cornell's auditioned jazz ensemble builds musicianship, improvisation, and ensemble skills while studying the cultural and historical contexts of jazz.
facts.hook: builds improvisation and ensemble skills for auditioned jazz players
facts.quote: Jazz Ensemble (MUSIC 4615) ... The Jazz Ensemble develops musicianship, improvisation, and ensemble skills while exploring the cultural and historical contexts of the art form. ... Participation is by audition.
facts.sourceTitle: Jazz | Department of Music
facts.commonnessReason: Most universities have a jazz ensemble.

facts.title: Jazz+
facts.summary: A student jazz organization open to everyone that runs jam sessions, master classes, and guest artist performances and manages a gig referral service.
facts.hook: organizes jam sessions, master classes, and a gig referral service for student musicians
facts.quote: Jazz+ is a student organization dedicated to the appreciation and performance of jazz music plus more. ... Jazz+ is open to everyone. Officers and members coordinate jam sessions, social events, master classes, and performances by guest artists. The org manages a gig referral service for student groups and helps manage performance and studio equipment.
facts.sourceTitle: Jazz | Department of Music

facts.title: Society of Hispanic Professional Engineers, Cornell Chapter
facts.nameOnPage: Society of Hispanic Professional Engineers, Cornell Chapter
facts.summary: The Cornell chapter of the Society of Hispanic Professional Engineers works to increase the participation of Hispanic students and professionals in engineering, science, and math.
facts.hook: connects Hispanic engineering students to a professional community in engineering and science
facts.quote: Dedicated to increasing the participation of Hispanic professionals and college students in the fields of engineering, science, and math.
facts.sourceTitle: Undergraduate Experience | School of Civil and Environmental Engineering | Cornell Duffield Engineering
facts.commonnessReason: SHPE chapters exist at many engineering schools.

facts.title: The Cornell Daily Sun
facts.summary: Cornell's student newspaper, founded in 1880, is independent of the university and staffed almost entirely by Cornell students from an office in downtown Ithaca.
facts.hook: is staffed almost entirely by students, who run an independent paper founded in 1880
facts.quote: Founded in 1880, The Cornell Daily Sun is the oldest continuously independent college daily newspaper in the country. It is staffed almost entirely by Cornell students, operating out of an office building in downtown Ithaca.
facts.sourceTitle: Does Cornell have a student newspaper? - Frequently Asked Questions
facts.commonnessReason: Every campus has a student paper; known but rarely the center of an essay.

facts.title: Translator Interpreter Program (TIP)
facts.summary: A student-run program at Cornell's Language Resource Center that trains bilingual and multilingual volunteers to translate and interpret for community agencies.
facts.hook: trains bilingual students to interpret and translate for local community agencies
facts.quote: The LRC's Translator Interpreter Program (TIP) is the oldest and largest faculty-approved, student-run translation and interpretation program in the United States. TIP trains bilingual and multilingual Cornell volunteers to become translators and interpreters for both emergency and non-emergency situations of community agencies.
facts.sourceTitle: Student Organizations | Language Resource Center

facts.title: Campus as a Living Laboratory
facts.summary: Cornell opens its campus energy and water systems for study: solar farms share real-time data, and students can tour and work with staff at the Central Energy Plant and water filtration plant.
facts.hook: opens campus solar farm data and energy and water plants to student projects
facts.quote: Our solar farms have open data-platforms to study real-time data, and campus community members can tour and work with staff in the Central Energy Plant, water filtration plant, and more. By using real-world systems for course study and projects, our students and staff can learn about sustainability innovation on our campus and help improve our systems in real time.
facts.sourceTitle: Living Laboratory | Sustainable Cornell

facts.title: Community Learning and Service Partnership (CLASP)
facts.summary: An Einhorn Center program that pairs students with Cornell employees each semester for learning partnerships, most often English for Speakers of Other Languages.
facts.hook: pairs students with Cornell employees in learning partnerships, most often English language practice
facts.quote: They were among the roughly 40 employee-student learning partnerships brought together each semester through the Community Learning and Service Partnership (CLASP). ... English for Speakers of Other Languages is the most commonly requested area of study, followed by computer skills, but goals vary widely, from studying for the GED to learning an instrument or improving health and wellness.
facts.sourceTitle: CLASP joins Einhorn Center, expanding employee-student learning partnerships – Einhorn Center for Community Engagement

facts.title: Cornell in Washington (DC Connect)
facts.summary: Cornell in Washington lets students live and learn in Washington, D.C.; its DC Connect Spring program is open to all upper-level Cornell students.
facts.hook: lets upper-level students live and learn in Washington, D.C., through DC Connect
facts.quote: Students live and learn in the heart of Washington, D.C., while enjoying the support of our experienced residence life team. ... DC Connect Spring ... Open to all upper-level Cornell students
facts.sourceTitle: Brooks DC Programs - Cornell Brooks Public Policy
facts.commonnessReason: A well-known Cornell off-campus program for policy-minded students.

facts.title: Cornell Outdoor Education
facts.summary: Cornell Outdoor Education offers wilderness trips, adventure programs, and outdoor courses for students.
facts.hook: takes students into the wilderness through outdoor courses and adventure trips
facts.quote: Discover the wilderness, experience new adventures, and explore the world. Cornell offers the most comprehensive collegiate outdoor education program in the country.
facts.sourceTitle: Health & Wellness | Undergraduate Admissions
facts.commonnessReason: Featured on admissions pages and widely cited by applicants who love the outdoors.

facts.title: DC Start
facts.summary: A first-semester residential program in Washington, D.C., for first-year Brooks School students entering the public policy and health care policy majors.
facts.hook: starts first-year Brooks students' policy studies in Washington, D.C.
facts.quote: DC Start is a residential academic experience offered to first year Brooks School undergraduate students in their fall semester. Housed at the Brooks School’s Wolpe Building in close walking distance to Dupont Circle in Washington D.C., the program offers an inspiring, immersive public policy learning experience to students entering the public policy and health care policy majors.
facts.sourceTitle: First-Year Undergrads - Cornell Brooks Public Policy
facts.commonnessReason: Featured in the Brooks School admissions requirements.

facts.title: eLab
facts.summary: Cornell's student business accelerator, which admits many student teams in the fall and narrows the cohort in the spring as teams build their companies.
facts.hook: runs a fall-to-spring accelerator cohort for student startups
facts.quote: eLab is a student accelerator that launches several businesses each year. ... A large number of student teams are welcomed in the fall semester and the cohort is narrowed in the spring based off a pre-determined rubric instructors use to evaluate teams’ performance and business models.
facts.sourceTitle: eLab - Entrepreneurship at Cornell
facts.commonnessReason: Student accelerators are common; eLab is known among entrepreneurship applicants.

facts.title: Global Start Cantabria
facts.summary: A Duffield Engineering program in which first-year students spend their first semester in Santander, Spain, after two weeks of immersion Spanish with a host family.
facts.hook: lets first-year engineers start in Santander, Spain, with immersion Spanish and a host family
facts.quote: Duffield Engineering Global Start participants will take a similar course load as their counterparts starting their first term at Cornell. ... As part of the Global Start Cantabria Program, all students will take intensive immersion Spanish for two weeks and live with a host family prior to the start of classes.
facts.sourceTitle: Global Start Cantabria | Cornell Duffield Engineering
facts.commonnessReason: Featured on the admissions page for engineering applicants.

facts.title: Laidlaw Leadership and Research Program
facts.summary: A two-year cohort program for first- and second-year students from any college that supports leadership development, research, and a summer abroad putting skills into action.
facts.hook: supports early undergraduates with leadership training, research, and a summer abroad
facts.quote: With generous support for your leadership development, a summer abroad putting your skills into action, and research, this two-year cohort program for emerging leaders lays out a path for you to invest your skills, knowledge, and experience to make global change. ... First- and second-year students from any college or major may apply.
facts.sourceTitle: Laidlaw Leadership and Research Program | Einaudi Center

facts.title: NYSWRI Summer Student Research Program
facts.summary: A paid summer internship of about ten weeks, open to any Cornell student, on water projects such as emerging contaminants, watershed resilience, water governance, and water infrastructure.
facts.hook: offers paid summer water research internships on contaminants, watersheds, and infrastructure
facts.quote: Intern applications are solicited from any Cornell University undergraduate or graduate student. ... Summer internships last for approximately ten weeks. ... This unique set of paid summer intern projects deal with issues such as micropollutants and emerging contaminants, watershed resilience to climate change, water resource governance, sustainable water infrastructure, and environmental justice.
facts.sourceTitle: Summer Student Research Program | CALS

facts.title: Pre-Orientation Service Trips (POST)
facts.summary: A pre-orientation program in which incoming students do daily community service projects in Ithaca and Tompkins County while transitioning to Cornell.
facts.hook: starts incoming students with community service projects around Ithaca and Tompkins County
facts.quote: POST offers a unique opportunity for incoming students to explore and engage with the Ithaca and Tompkins County communities while transitioning to college life at Cornell. The program includes daily community-service projects, learning about pressing community issues and participation in fun group evening events.
facts.sourceTitle: Pre-Orientation Service Trips (POST) – Einhorn Center for Community Engagement

facts.title: Rising Researchers Program
facts.summary: A Duffield Engineering program that matches first- and second-year undergraduates with graduate student mentors for spring and summer research projects.
facts.hook: pairs first- and second-year engineers with graduate mentors for spring and summer research
facts.quote: First and second year Duffield Engineering undergrads who participate in at least one Office of Inclusive Excellence research event and attend two research group open houses/tours are eligible to apply for a mentored research position as a Rising Researcher beginning in the spring. During the spring and summer, undergraduates work on a research project in close collaboration with a graduate student mentor.
facts.sourceTitle: Rising Researchers Program | Cornell Duffield Engineering

facts.title: Cornell Chimes
facts.summary: Bells in McGraw Tower mark every fifteen minutes and ring daily concerts played by the student-run Cornell Chimes, whose chimesmasters are student and alumni musicians.
facts.hook: fills campus with daily bell concerts played by student chimesmasters in McGraw Tower
facts.quote: Cornell’s chimes are housed in McGraw Tower, which is attached to the library. Every fifteen minutes, bells mark the passing of time, and two or three times a day, the campus is treated to a bell concert ... The Cornell Chimes is a student-run organization, and the chimesmasters themselves are student and alumni musicians who bring music to the campus every day.
facts.sourceTitle: Cornell Chimes | Uris Historical Tour - Online exhibitions across Cornell University Library
facts.commonnessReason: An iconic Cornell tradition that many applicants mention.

facts.title: Dragon Day
facts.summary: Each spring, first-year architecture students parade a giant dragon across campus to the Arts Quad, where it meets a phoenix built by engineering students.
facts.hook: pits a dragon built by first-year architects against a phoenix built by engineering students
facts.quote: Every year around St. Patrick's Day, an enormous dragon created by first-year architecture students parades across campus. Accompanied by architecture students in outrageous costumes, the dragon lumbers to the Arts Quad where it is slain by a phoenix created by rival engineering students.
facts.sourceTitle: The Cornell Experience | Undergraduate Admissions
facts.commonnessReason: One of Cornell's best-known traditions, featured on admissions pages.

facts.title: Slope Day
facts.summary: Every May before finals, thousands of students gather on Libe Slope for a day of music and celebration, a tradition that began as Spring Day in 1902.
facts.hook: brings thousands of students to Libe Slope for music and celebration before finals
facts.quote: Every May, before the start of final exams, thousands of students gather on Libe Slope for a day of music, fun, and celebration. ... A Cornell tradition for more than 100 years, it started in 1902 when the university declared “Spring Day” a campus-wide holiday.
facts.sourceTitle: Slope Day
facts.commonnessReason: Cornell's best-known annual celebration, named on admissions pages.
